bib.title: Extracting Training Data from Large Language Models

question: Can an adversary with black-box query access recover verbatim individual training examples from a large language model trained on a large, little-overfit corpus?
hypothesis: Even though large LMs show almost no train/test gap, worst-case training examples are memorized and can be extracted.
contributions: Define k-eidetic memorization and a black-box threat model
A two-step attack: diverse sampling then membership-inference ranking against a reference (smaller LM, zlib, lowercase, sliding window)
Extract 604 verbatim GPT-2 training examples including PII, UUIDs, code
Analysis of how model size and insertion frequency affect memorization

method.summary: Generate 200,000 256-token samples from GPT-2 XL under each of three sampling strategies, rank each set by six membership-inference metrics, take 100 per configuration from the top 1000 after fuzzy dedup, and verify by Google search and by the GPT-2 authors' check against the training set.

datasets.name: GPT-2 training data (WebText, Reddit outbound links)
datasets.split: not released; GPT-2 authors gave limited query access
datasets.source: scraped from links followed from Reddit, document-level dedup, trained ~12 epochs (personal communication)
datasets.preprocessing: HTML removed, dedup at document level

datasets.name: Common Crawl subset (attack prefixes)
datasets.split: 5 to 10 random tokens per sample used as prefix
datasets.preprocessing: HTML and JavaScript removed, line-by-line dedup

inference.decoding: top-n sampling with n=40; beam-search-like decoding (Carlini 2019) for extending sequences and Table 4 easier variant
inference.temperature: 1 for top-n and Internet; temperature strategy decays from t=10 to t=1 over first 20 tokens (~10% of sequence)
inference.samples: 200,000 samples per sampling strategy (3 strategies, 600,000 total); 100 selected per config (1,800 total); 10,000 generations per model for Table 4 URL test
inference.prompting: top-n and temperature: one-token start-of-sentence prompt; Internet: 5 to 10 random tokens from Common Crawl

parameters.sliding window: 50 tokens, chosen after a cursory hyper-parameter sweep
parameters.selection: 100 from top-1000 with fraction of selected samples below rank k equal to sqrt(k/1000)

metrics.name: memorized count / true positive rate
metrics.definition: candidate counts as memorized if a non-trivial substring exactly matches a Google result, and the GPT-2 authors' fuzzy 3-gram match on the training set confirms

metrics.name: membership inference ranking metrics
metrics.definition: Perplexity, Small and Medium (ratio of log perplexities vs smaller GPT-2), zlib (ratio of log GPT-2 perplexity to zlib entropy), Lowercase (ratio of perplexity original vs lowercased), Window (min perplexity over 50-token windows)

baselines: top-n sampling with plain perplexity ranking (Sec 4)
eval.protocol: One of four authors manually labelled each of 1,800 candidates by Google search; confirmed with OpenAI via fuzzy 3-gram match (no false negatives, some false positives); single run, no seeds or confidence intervals stated.

evidence.quote: Speciﬁcally, we use the Small (117M parameters) and Medium (345M parameters) models.

results.claim: 604 unique memorized training examples found among 1,800 inspected candidates
results.setup: GPT-2 XL, 3 sampling x 6 ranking configs, 100 candidates each, 200,000 samples per sampling strategy, manual Google match plus OpenAI 3-gram check
results.quote:
we identify 604 unique memo-
rized training examples from among the 1,800 possible can-
didates, for an aggregate true positive rate of 33.5%

results.claim: Aggregate true positive rate over the 1,800 candidates
results.quote:
for an aggregate true positive rate of 33.5% (our best
variant has a true positive rate of 67%)

results.claim: Best configuration (Internet conditioning ranked by zlib) has 67 of 100 candidates memorized
results.setup: GPT-2 XL, Internet (Common Crawl prefix) sampling, zlib ratio ranking
results.quote:
For example, 67% of
Internet samples marked by zlib are memorized.

results.claim: Plain perplexity ranking is a poor membership inference metric for top-n and temperature sampling
results.setup: GPT-2 XL, perplexity ranking, top-n sampling (9) and temperature sampling (3)
results.quote:
just 9% and
3% of inspected samples are memorized, respectively

results.claim: Top-n baseline yields 191 unique memorized samples; Internet conditioning yields 273
results.setup: GPT-2 XL, Internet vs top-n sampling, all six rankings pooled
results.quote:
yields 191 unique memorized samples, whereas
conditioning on Internet text increases this to 273

results.claim: Full-size GPT-2 emits every Reddit URL inserted 33 or more times in one document; Small memorizes none under the harder attack
results.setup: 10,000 top-n generations from a fixed URL prefix, GPT-2 XL 1.5B; Medium 345M got half, Small 117M none
results.quote:
the full-sized 1.5 billion
parameter GPT-2 model emits all examples that are inserted
33 times or more

results.claim: Larger models memorize more: 1.5B GPT-2 memorizes over 18x as much content as the 124M model in one setting
results.quote:
the 1.5 billion parameter GPT-2 model memorizes
over 18× as much content as the 124 million parameter model

results.claim: GPT-2 trained about 12 epochs on 40GB, train loss only ~10% below test loss
results.source: Personal communication with the GPT-2 authors; Radford et al. 2019
results.quote:
the training loss is only
roughly 10% smaller than the test loss across all model sizes

results.claim: At least 0.1% of 600,000 honest generations contain memorized text (loose lower bound)
results.quote:
among 600,000 (honestly) generated samples, our attacks
ﬁnd that at least 604 (or 0.1%) contain memorized text

results.claim: Memorized content in 46 samples names individuals and 32 hold contact info (16 business, 16 private)
results.quote:
We ﬁnd 46 examples that contain individual peoples’
names.

results.claim: Memorized high-entropy strings with k=1 up to 87 characters long, 10 occurrences in one document
results.quote:
we extract a 87-characters-long sequence that is contained in the training
dataset just 10 times in total, all in the same document

results.claim: Beam-search extension recovers a 1450-line verbatim source file
results.setup: seeded with a memorized snippet, beam-search-like decoding from Carlini 2019
results.quote: namely 1450 lines of verbatim source code

results.claim: Context matters: GPT-2 greedy gives 25 digits of pi from '3.14159', 799 with 'pi is 3.14159', 824 with extra context, 500 with beam search
results.setup: greedy decoding with prompt 'e begins 2.7182818, pi begins 3.14159'
results.quote: GPT-2 greedily completes the ﬁrst 824 digits of π

results.claim: Harvested GPT-2 attack is a lower bound; none of 273 Internet-conditioned extractions reproduce reliably from the original short prefix
results.quote:
None of the 273 extracted samples found using Internet
conditioning can be reliably reproduced when using the same
preﬁx initially provided to GPT-2

limits: Manual evaluation by four authors over only 1,800 candidates; the 604 is a lower bound, recall over the whole training set is not measured
Memorization is prefix dependent, simple prompts under-estimate it
Single model family (GPT-2) with training data that is public; text domain only
Verification uses fuzzy 3-gram match with false positives
Results cannot say if bigger models of other families behave alike; no mitigation is evaluated
Definition 1 admits pathological cases such as 'Repeat the following sentence'

terms.definition: A string s is k-eidetic memorized by an LM if s is extractable and s appears in at most k examples in the training data
A string s is extractable from an LM if there exists a prefix c such that s is the argmax continuation of length N
